scenes.title: Practical Numerical Engineering
scenes.purpose: Practical Numerical Engineering: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Practical Numerical Engineering: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Earlier binomial tree models assumed continuous dividend yields, but real-world equities pay discrete, lump-sum cash dividends.

hi.display: Sharma ji, previous chapters mein humne binomial trees padhe jahan stock continuous dividend yield deta tha. Lekin real companies cash dividend fixed dollar amount mein deti hain. Ye practical dividend tree par kaise model hota hai?

en.display: These discrete cash dividend drops break lattice recombination, causing an exponential two-to-the-N node explosion that overwhelms memory.

hi.display: Raju, discrete dollar dividend aate hi standard binomial tree completely collapse ho jata hai! Agar hum naive tree banayein, toh ex-dividend drop ki wajah se nodes aapas mein recombine nahi hote, aur nodes ki sankhya exponentially explode kar jaati hai.

en.display: In Chapter 21 Part 1, we master John Hull's stock price decomposition to restore recombination, and construct three-branch Trinomial Trees.

hi.display: Aaj Chapter 21 mein hum dekhenge ki John Hull ne is non-recombining crisis ko solve karne ke liye Stock Decomposition method kaise invent kiya, aur kaise Trinomial Trees extra stability provide karte hain!

scenes.title: The Non-Recombining Tree Dilemma
scenes.purpose: The Non-Recombining Tree Dilemma: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: The Non-Recombining Tree Dilemma: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Observe the mathematical failure: an up move followed by dividend deduction and a down move produces (S_0 u - D) times d.

hi.display: Mathematical problem ko dhyan se dekhiye: Maan lijiye stock par up move ke baad dividend D deduct hota hai, aur fir down move hota hai. Toh price banta hai S zero u minus D times d.

en.display: Conversely, a down move followed by dividend deduction and an up move yields (S_0 d - D) times u. These two nodal values are not equal!

hi.display: Lekin agar pehle down move ho aur fir dividend deduct hoke up move ho, toh price banta hai S zero d minus D times u. Ye dono values mathematical equal nahi hoteen!

en.display: Because nodes do not recombine, after 30 time steps the tree explodes into over one billion nodes, rendering calculation impossible.

hi.display: Iska result ye hota hai ki tree recombine nahi hota. 30 time steps ke baad tree mein 2 ki power 30 yaani 1 billion se zyada nodes ban jayenge! Kisi bhi computer ke liye is path-dependent explosion ko calculate karna impossible ho jata hai.

scenes.title: Hull's Stock Price Decomposition
scenes.purpose: Hull's Stock Price Decomposition: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Hull's Stock Price Decomposition: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: To defeat this exponential explosion, John Hull formulated a powerful decomposition dividing stock price S(t) into two distinct parts.

hi.display: Is exponential explosion ko defeat karne ke liye John Hull ne ek brilliant mathematical decomposition invent kiya: hum stock price S of t ko do parts mein split karte hain.

en.display: The first part is the Riskless Component: the discounted present value of all scheduled future cash dividends payable during option life.

hi.display: Pehla part hai Riskless Component, jo future mein aane wale sabhi scheduled dividends ki discounted present value hota hai.

en.display: The second part is the Stochastic Component S*(t): an uncertain diffusion process that follows standard geometric Brownian motion.

hi.display: Aur dusra part hai Stochastic Component S star of t, jo stock ka uncertain, volatile hissa hota hai aur continuous geometric Brownian motion follow karta hai.

scenes.title: Recombining Lattice on S*
scenes.purpose: Recombining Lattice on S*: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Recombining Lattice on S*: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: The core breakthrough is that we construct the lattice not on actual stock S, but strictly on stochastic component S*.

hi.display: Screen par dekhiye: ab hum pura binomial tree actual stock S par nahi, balki stochastic component S star par construct karte hain.

en.display: Because S* pays no dividends during the step, the condition u times d equals one holds identically, ensuring perfect lattice recombination!

hi.display: Kyunki S star khud koi dividend pay nahi karta, iska up step u aur down step d hamesha multiply hoke 1 banate hain. Isse tree perfectly recombine karta hai!

en.display: At 30 steps, instead of one billion nodes, only 496 recombining nodes are generated. Adding remaining dividend present value recovers true stock S(t).

hi.display: 30 steps par 1 billion nodes ke bajay, sirf 496 recombining nodes bante hain. Aur har node par hum PV of remaining dividends add karke true market stock price S of t recover kar lete hain.

scenes.title: Nodal Early Exercise with S(t)
scenes.purpose: Nodal Early Exercise with S(t): Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Nodal Early Exercise with S(t): Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Option valuation proceeds via standard backward induction, using true terminal stock price S_T at maturity to compute payoffs.

hi.display: Option valuation ke liye backward induction standard tareeqe se chalta hai. Terminal maturity par true stock price S of T use hota hai.

en.display: At each intermediate node, American exercise value is evaluated directly against true stock price S(t) rather than artificial S*.

hi.display: Har intermediate node par American option holder ke paas do choices hoti hain: continue karna ya immediate early exercise karna. Yahan intrinsic value hamesha true stock price S of t se calculate hoti hai.

en.display: The nodal rule is: Value equals maximum of Intrinsic Value at S(t) and Continuation Value. Hull's model captures exact early exercise timing!

hi.display: Nodal rule: Node Value equals maximum of intrinsic value S of t minus K, aur discounted expected continuation value. Hull ka decomposition tree ko recombining banaye rakhte hue exact American early exercise timing capture kar leta hai!

scenes.title: Multi-Asset Tree Generalization
scenes.purpose: Multi-Asset Tree Generalization: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Multi-Asset Tree Generalization: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: The binomial tree architecture extends seamlessly across all major asset classes by adjusting growth parameter a.

hi.display: Ab agar asset discrete dollar dividend ke bajay continuous dividend yield q pay kare—jaise stock indices—toh recombining tree directly apply hota hai jahan growth parameter a equals e to the power r minus q delta t hota hai.

en.display: For continuous dividend yield q, parameter a equals e to the power (r - q) delta t; for currencies, a equals e to the (r - r_f) delta t.

hi.display: Foreign currencies ke liye parameter a equals e to the power r minus r f delta t hota hai, jahan r f foreign risk-free interest rate hai.

en.display: And for futures options, parameter a is identically 1.0000, reflecting zero expected drift in the risk-neutral measure.

hi.display: Aur commodity futures contracts ke liye parameter a exactly 1 hota hai, kyunki risk-neutral world mein futures price ka drift zero hota hai.

scenes.title: Trinomial Trees: Three-Branch Architecture
scenes.purpose: Trinomial Trees: Three-Branch Architecture: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Trinomial Trees: Three-Branch Architecture: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Now let us examine an advanced numerical framework: Trinomial Trees, featuring three distinct branches: Up, Middle, and Down.

hi.display: Ab chaliye advanced lattice architecture par: Trinomial Trees. Yahan har node se do nahi, balki teen branches nikalte hain: Up, Middle, aur Down!

en.display: The up factor is u = e^(sigma * sqrt(3 * dt)), the middle factor is m = 1, and the down factor is d = 1 / u.

hi.display: Up branch factor hota hai u equals e to the power sigma square root 3 delta t, middle branch factor m equals 1 yaani no price change, aur down factor d equals 1 upon u.

en.display: Risk-neutral probabilities p_u, p_m = 2/3, and p_d match continuous drift and variance with extraordinary numerical precision.

hi.display: Teeno branches ki risk-neutral probabilities p u, p m equals 2 by 3, aur p d mathematically continuous drift aur variance ko exactly match karti hain.

scenes.title: Why Trinomial Trees Outperform Binomial Trees
scenes.purpose: Why Trinomial Trees Outperform Binomial Trees: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Why Trinomial Trees Outperform Binomial Trees: Foundational quantitative principles

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Why do trinomial trees outperform binomial trees in quantitative production? First, the three-branch design guarantees positive probabilities.

hi.display: Trinomial trees binomial models se superior kyu hain? Pehla reason: extra branch ki wajah se probabilities hamesha positive rehti hain aur extreme volatility par negative probability error nahi aata.

beats.onScreenIntent: Why Trinomial Trees Outperform Binomial Trees

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Second, fixing central probability p_m at 2/3 completely dampens the odd-even numerical oscillations seen in binomial lattices.

hi.display: Dusra reason: Central probability p m ko 2 by 3 par fix karne se numerical oscillations completely suppress ho jaati hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Why Trinomial Trees Outperform Binomial Trees

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Third, a trinomial tree is mathematically identical to an explicit finite difference scheme for solving the Black-Scholes PDE!

hi.display: Teesra aur sabse important point: Trinomial tree mathematically Black-Scholes partial differential equation ke explicit finite difference method ke completely equivalent hota hai!

scenes.title: Worked Example: 2-Step Trinomial Tree
scenes.purpose: Worked Example: 2-Step Trinomial Tree: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Worked Example: 2-Step Trinomial Tree: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Let us calculate a concrete worked example: S_0 = $100, strike K = $100, r = 5%, volatility = 20%, and T = 0.5 years across two steps.

hi.display: Sharma ji, kya hum actual numbers ke sath ek trinomial tree solve karke dekh sakte hain?

en.display: With delta t = 0.25 years, step factor u = 1.1904, d = 0.8401, and p_m = 0.6667, five distinct terminal price levels emerge.

hi.display: Zaroor! Maan lijiye S zero equals 100 dollars, strike K equals 100 dollars, risk-free rate 5 percent, volatility 20 percent, aur maturity 6 months hai do time steps ke sath.

en.display: Backward induction yields an American put value of $3.98, converging within 2% of the continuous Black-Scholes benchmark in just two steps!

hi.display: Step size calculate karte hain: u equals 1.1904, d equals 0.8401, aur central probability p m 0.6667 hai. Terminal period t equals 0.5 par 5 price levels bante hain: 141.7, 119.0, 100.0, 84.0, aur 70.6 dollars.

en.display: Evaluate the scenario: Stock trades at $54, call strike is $50. Tomorrow is ex-dividend with a $2.00 cash dividend. Exercise today or hold? Consider the options on screen.

hi.display: Backward induction apply karne par American Put option ki fair value 3.98 dollars aati hai. Sirf 2 trinomial steps mein hum exact continuous Black-Scholes value ke behad kareeb pahunch gaye!

scenes.title: Interactive Cognitive Quiz
scenes.purpose: Interactive Cognitive Quiz: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Interactive Cognitive Quiz: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Pause and calculate: Compare immediate intrinsic value against expected post-dividend price and continuation value.

hi.display: Raju, ab ek critical real-world trading quiz: Ek investor ke paas 50 dollar strike American Call option hai, aur stock price 54 dollars hai. Kal company ka ex-dividend date hai jahan 2 dollar cash dividend pay hoga. Kya investor ko aaj market close hone se pehle call exercise karni chahiye ya hold karna chahiye?

en.display: Option A is correct: Exercise today! Immediate exercise locks in $4.00 profit. Holding past ex-date drops stock to $52, reducing intrinsic value to $2.00 permanently!

hi.display: Is mathematical concept aur financial derivation ko dhyan se samajhiye.

en.display: Standard trees assume constant volatility, but real option markets exhibit volatility smiles and downward skews.

hi.display: Correct answer hai Option A: Investor ko aaj hi early exercise karna chahiye! Aaj exercise karne par 4 dollar intrinsic cash milta hai. Agar kal tak hold kiya, toh stock drop hokar 52 dollar ho jayega aur intrinsic value gir kar sirf 2 dollar reh jayegi, jisse dividend ka 2 dollar loss permanently ho jayega!

data.question: Which statement accurately describes the core derivatives principle?
options: The equilibrium condition holds via continuous risk-neutral replication.
Expected asset drift determines contingent claim value directly.
Arbitrage bounds can be systematically violated in liquid markets.
Discrete binomial tree steps eliminate all underlying price variance.
data.explanation: Risk-neutral replication eliminates subjective risk preferences from derivatives pricing.

scenes.title: Summary: 8 Rules of Practical Trees
scenes.purpose: Summary: 8 Rules of Practical Trees: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Summary: 8 Rules of Practical Trees: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Rule 1: Discrete dividends cause non-recombining exponential node explosion; Rule 2: Hull's S* decomposition restores perfect recombination.

hi.display: Chaliye Chapter 21 Part 1 ke 8 core quantitative rules ko consolidate karte hain: Rule 1 — Discrete cash dividends standard binomial trees ko non-recombining bana kar exponential node explosion create karte hain. Rule 2 — Hull Stock Decomposition stock ko S star stochastic component aur dividend present value mein split karke recombination restore karta hai.

en.display: Rule 3: Growth parameter a unifies equities, currencies, and futures; Rule 4: Trinomial trees use three branches with u = e^(sigma sqrt(3 dt)).

hi.display: Rule 3 — Multi-asset parameter a tree ko stock dividend yield, foreign currencies, aur futures ke sath seamlessly unify karta hai. Rule 4 — Trinomial trees up, middle, aur down branches ke sath 3-state lattice form karte hain.

en.display: Rule 5: Trinomial trees suppress odd-even lattice oscillations; Rule 6: Trinomial lattices are mathematically equivalent to explicit PDE schemes.

hi.display: Rule 5 — Trinomial step size u equals e to the power sigma square root 3 delta t variance ko preserve karta hai aur p m equals 2 by 3 stability provide karta hai. Rule 6 — Trinomial tree explicit finite difference PDE solver ke mathematically identical hota hai.

en.display: Rule 7: Deep ITM calls must be exercised before ex-dividend dates; Rule 8: Implied trees calibrate local probabilities to empirical volatility smiles.

hi.display: Rule 7 — American calls on dividend-paying stocks must be evaluated for early exercise immediately prior to ex-dividend dates. Rule 8 — Implied binomial and trinomial trees calibrate local probabilities to match live market volatility smiles.

en.display: These eight principles master practical tree engineering and form the bridge to continuous finite difference methods.

hi.display: Screen par summary table mein sabhi governing formulas aur lattice algorithms systematically compile kar diye gaye hain.

en.display: In the next video, we begin Chapter 21 Part 2: Monte Carlo Simulation and Finite Difference Methods!

hi.display: Agli video mein hum shuru karenge Chapter 21 Part 2: Monte Carlo Simulation aur Finite Difference Methods. Practice jari rakhiye!
